overall_summary: Crypto faces clear headwinds today from heavy ETF outflows, large liquidations, and hawkish Fed signals pointing to further tightening. A Trump comment ruling out Iran strikes sparked a short-lived bounce, and Thailand’s ETF rules are a bright spot, but the broader tone stays risk-off with a firm dollar and tight labor data. Traders should watch whether support holds or more selling follows.
key_points: Bitcoin ETFs bleed nearly $730M in two days
Fed speakers and minutes lean hawkish on hikes
Trump rules out Iran strike, brief BTC bounce
Thailand finalizes local Bitcoin and Ether ETFs
Over $1.2B liquidations as BTC dips under $81K

items.title: Crypto Sees $1.2B Liquidations as BTC Dips Under $81K
items.summary: Leveraged longs got crushed with over one billion dollars in liquidations across crypto in twenty-four hours, mostly bullish bets. Ether took the worst hit at roughly three hundred fifty million, about six times Bitcoin's rate relative to size, while Bitcoin itself saw nearly three hundred million wiped. Price briefly broke under eighty-one thousand before bouncing. Traders should care because the flush cleared a lot of leverage and tested key support; if it holds, the market can stabilize, but further macro pressure could force another leg down.
items.impact: Short-term volatility with potential stabilization if support holds

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Bleed Nearly $730M Over Two Sessions
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about four hundred eighty-five million in outflows on October seventh, the biggest daily hit since June, followed by another two hundred forty-four million on the eighth. Fidelity and BlackRock led the exits. Ether ETFs extended a multi-day outflow streak, pushing combined October redemptions toward one billion. This matters because ETF flows are a primary institutional demand signal; sustained selling removes a key bid and adds supply pressure on Bitcoin near current levels.
items.impact: Adds selling pressure and weakens near-term demand support

items.title: US Government Moves Over $1.5B in Seized Bitcoin
items.summary: Wallets tied to US authorities transferred roughly seventeen thousand BTC worth about one point five billion dollars over three days, including twelve thousand two hundred sixty-seven BTC from Bitfinex hack seizures to new addresses and earlier batches into Coinbase Prime. No exchange sales were confirmed, and policy points to a strategic reserve rather than dumps. Traders care because large government moves often spark sell-off fears and supply overhang narratives even when they are just custody reshuffles.
items.impact: Sentiment overhang without confirmed selling pressure

items.title: Trump Rules Out Iran Strike, BTC Rebounds to $82.5K
items.summary: President Trump stated the US will not strike Iran before the November midterms, easing geopolitical fears that had pushed oil higher and dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin recovered from a low near eighty thousand three hundred to around eighty-two thousand five hundred. Oil prices pulled back in response. This is key for traders because it removed an immediate macro tail risk that was amplifying the selloff and liquidations, allowing a relief bounce in crypto.
items.impact: Supports short-term risk-on rebound and reduces oil-driven pressure

items.title: Thailand Finalizes Rules for Local Bitcoin and Ether ETFs
items.summary: Thailand's SEC issued rules effective October sixteenth allowing asset managers to list passive Bitcoin and Ether ETFs on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. Funds must hold at least eighty percent average exposure to one asset, use regulated local custodians, and cannot offer margin. Mutual funds can also invest in them. Traders should note this expands regulated Asian access and signals continued global ETF adoption, even if Thailand's market size means limited immediate flows.
items.impact: Positive long-term adoption signal with modest near-term flow potential

items.title: MARA Moves $81M Bitcoin to Galaxy Amid AI Pivot
items.summary: Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings transferred about nine hundred ninety-six BTC worth eighty-one million dollars to a Galaxy Digital address. The move does not confirm an immediate sale but fits a pattern of treasury reductions as the company shifts toward AI and high-performance computing; holdings have already fallen sharply this year after earlier sales. This adds to supply-watch lists for traders monitoring corporate and miner selling during a fragile price recovery.
items.impact: Potential incremental supply if sold into the market

items.title: Fed's Waller, Musalem Signal More Hikes Likely
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said additional rate increases will probably be needed to bring inflation back to two percent, though there is flexibility on timing and hikes need not come at consecutive meetings, leaving the door open for an October pause. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem echoed that more firming is required over the next six to nine months to hit the target in a timely way, while stressing he goes into the late-October meeting with an open mind. Markets are pricing low odds of an October move but solid chances of a December hike. Crypto traders should watch because higher-for-longer rates and sticky inflation keep pressure on risk assets and liquidity.
items.impact: Supports higher yields and firmer dollar, weighing on Bitcoin risk appetite

items.title: FOMC Minutes Confirm Bias for Further Tightening
items.summary: Minutes from the September FOMC meeting, released Wednesday and still driving discussion, showed a unanimous vote to hike rates to three point seven five to four percent. Most participants judged another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end, citing insufficient progress on inflation and upside risks from energy, demand, and possible tariffs. The dots already pointed that way, so the minutes largely reinforced the hawkish lean without forcing an immediate October move. Traders care because it anchors rate-cut hopes lower and keeps the higher-for-longer narrative alive into next week's data.
items.impact: Solidifies December hike odds and sustains elevated Treasury yields

items.title: Treasury Yields Ease After Solid 30-Year Auction
items.summary: The ten-year Treasury yield pulled back from multi-decade highs near five point three percent, closing around five point two three percent after a twenty-two billion dollar thirty-year bond auction drew solid demand with a two point five four bid-to-cover and high yield of five point six one eight percent. Term premium had climbed to twelve-year highs amid fiscal and inflation worries, but the auction relief and some yield decline offered temporary calm. Long-end moves matter for crypto because higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Short-term relief for risk assets if yields stabilize; still elevated levels remain a headwind

items.title: Jobless Claims Fall to 197k, Labor Still Tight
items.summary: Initial jobless claims dropped two thousand to one hundred ninety-seven thousand for the week ended October third, below the two hundred thousand forecast and the fourth straight week under that mark, near multi-decade lows. Continuing claims rose modestly to one point seven one six million. The data points to a low-hire, low-fire market that remains resilient even after soft September payrolls of just twenty-nine thousand. For markets this keeps the Fed focused on inflation rather than employment risks, supporting the case for further tightening if prices stay sticky.
items.impact: Resilient labor reduces recession fears but sustains hawkish Fed bias

items.title: Dollar Holds Near Multi-Month Highs Around 102
items.summary: The dollar index eased slightly but stayed near eighteen-month or multi-month highs around one hundred two point one to one hundred two point two after Fed minutes and official comments reinforced higher rate expectations. Strength has been fueled by rising Treasury yields and relative US growth resilience versus peers. A firm dollar typically pressures crypto and emerging-market assets by tightening global financial conditions and making dollar-denominated risk less attractive. Watch for any break higher or softer data that could reverse the bid.
items.impact: Firm DXY acts as headwind for Bitcoin and risk assets

items.title: UMich Sentiment Due Today; Oil Eases on Trump Iran Comment
items.summary: Preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment for October is scheduled for ten a.m. Eastern today, with expectations near forty-seven to forty-eight after September's weak forty-eight point one final and elevated inflation expectations. Separately, oil pulled back after President Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November midterms amid productive discussions, easing some supply-risk premium that had pushed Brent above one hundred dollars. Soft sentiment or sticky inflation expectations could reinforce Fed caution, while cheaper oil helps the disinflation narrative. Both feed directly into rate-path pricing that crypto watches closely.
items.impact: Data and oil move could swing near-term rate expectations either way

items.title: Trump Rules Out Iran Strikes Before Midterms
items.summary: President Trump posted that the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms, citing productive discussions with Tehran while keeping the naval blockade in place. This came after reports the Pentagon was prepping options for pre-election strikes and as Iran reviewed a proposal to reopen Hormuz. Oil prices, which had spiked on escalation fears, pulled back. Traders should care because it temporarily lowers the risk of a major Middle East flare-up that has kept energy prices elevated and pressured risk assets including crypto via inflation and rate fears.
items.impact: Short-term risk-on relief and oil price moderation

items.title: Houthis Kill 3 in Riyadh Airport Missile Strikes
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, killing three including a Saudia pilot, damaging a plane, and forcing widespread flight cancellations. The attacks form part of an escalating war with Saudi-backed forces as Houthis push for Red Sea control and threaten oil sites. Saudi coalition hit back at launchers. This matters for traders as it widens the Iran war spillover, threatens more Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping, and keeps oil risk premiums elevated heading into winter.
items.impact: Higher oil volatility and regional risk premium

items.title: Russia Kills 33 in Kramatorsk Bus Strike
items.summary: A Russian guided bomb hit two passenger buses in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk, killing at least 33 civilians and wounding 18 in one of the deadliest single attacks this year. President Zelensky called it a deliberate strike on a bus stop and accused the US of inaction as nearly 80 died in two days of Russian assaults. Public transport was halted in key cities. Crypto traders watch this because sustained Ukraine escalation keeps global risk sentiment fragile, complicates energy and sanctions dynamics, and can drive safe-haven flows away from risk assets.

items.title: Oil Spikes Then Eases on War and Hurricane Risks
items.summary: Brent crude settled up over 4 percent near 104 dollars on Thursday on peak Hormuz tanker attacks, Houthi threats, potential Iran strikes, and Hurricane Isaias shutting in about 1.3 million barrels per day of US Gulf output. Prices retreated Friday after Trump's no-strike pledge and talk of Hormuz reopening proposals, though still elevated. Fresh US sanctions hit Iranian oil vessels. Energy shocks like this feed inflation, delay rate cuts, and typically weigh on Bitcoin and equities until resolved.
items.impact: Volatile energy prices keeping inflation and rate fears alive

items.title: US Hits Iran with Fresh Oil Shipping Sanctions
items.summary: The US Treasury imposed new sanctions targeting individuals, networks, and 17 vessels involved in moving Iranian crude, oil products, and petrochemicals. This comes as the blockade continues and despite diplomatic talk. It aims to tighten economic pressure amid the ongoing war. For markets, it sustains disruption to global oil flows and raises the chance of further Iranian retaliation in Hormuz, supporting higher energy prices that act as a headwind for risk assets.
items.impact: Sustained pressure on oil supply and shipping risk

items.title: Carrier Abraham Lincoln Returns from Iran War Duty
items.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group returned to San Diego after a nearly 11-month deployment, including a record stretch at sea supporting the US-Israel war on Iran. It conducted thousands of combat sorties, launched hundreds of Tomahawks, and helped enforce the blockade, earning a Presidential Unit Citation amid reports of crew strain. Its return underscores the war's duration and scale. Traders note it as a signal the conflict remains a multi-month drain on US resources and a lingering source of Middle East instability affecting energy and risk markets.
items.impact: Reminder of prolonged conflict without immediate de-escalation
